[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll do a quick intros and then go into the pilot scope, security constraints, and the ops runbook. Sound good?
[00:18] Tom (Caldera CTO): Yep, thanks. Quick context: we're spinning up an LLM feature in our developer platform, want to start with a small pilot around customer support triage, about 100-200 qps peak for a POC. Primary constraints are data residency, keys, and sub-300ms p50.
[00:30] Leah (Platform): Also our infra is mostly private k8s in our colo, we have a VPC peering setup and strict egress rules. We want either a private deployment or a very locked-down dedicated instance.
[00:45] Oliver (Redwood SE): Got it. We typically map that to Redwood Private for on-prem or VPC private control plane; Dedicated can work too if you need predictable throughput and we can lock down networking. Quick question on model sizes — are you planning small-medium open models or something heavier?
[01:05] Nina (PM): For the POC we want to try a 7B and a 13B variant, maybe a quantized 13B for cost checks. The quality bar is pretty high for triage accuracy, but we can trade some latency for accuracy.
[01:25] Raj (Security): From security, main asks: SOC2 evidence, audit log retention for 12 months, SSO via SAML/Okta, and KMS support where we control keys — ideally HSM-backed KMS. Also we need data at rest encryption and in-flight TLS.
[01:40] Aisha (CSM): Noted. We'll capture that and add to the onboarding checklist. Maya, I'll coordinate on the security packet.
[02:00] Maya: I'll send our SOC2 bundle and network diagram after the call — note: our Private deployment doc has the KMS patterns, but I will include an HSM option. Link: https://redwood.example.com/security-packet (placeholder).
[02:15] Tom: One practical thing — we want to run an internal smoke benchmark before the pilot. Can you outline what telemetry you'll need? CPU/GPU counters, latency percentiles, and token throughput?
[02:30] Oliver: Yes, we'll collect p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, GPU util, and memory/KV cache hit rates. For prefix caching we'd like to see how much hit rate we get on your typical session lengths. If you can share a sample workload (anonymized) that helps us tune batching and quantization suggestions.
[05:00] Leah: Our average seq length is about 350 tokens for the triage use case, but sometimes goes up to 1k for edge cases. We can provide traces and a sanitized sample.
[09:00] Maya: Let's talk about deployment tradeoffs — Hosted is fastest to start but less control over keys/residency; Dedicated gives predictability and can be isolated to a single tenant pool; Private gives you full VPC/on-prem control but longer lead time.
[09:30] Tom: We're leaning Private because of compliance; timeline is 6-8 weeks to pilot start if everything aligns. Are there prebuilt on-prem packages or do we orchestrate with your control plane?
[10:15] Oliver: We have a private control plane flow that talks to your VPC; for fully air-gapped there's an on-prem bundle that the infra team runs. It is a bit more hands-on. For the pilot, many customers do a hybrid — control plane in our managed env with model execution in your VPC.
[14:00] Raj: On audit logs — can we guarantee immutable logs for 12 months and export to our SIEM? We need to feed to Splunk.
[14:20] Aisha: You can configure log export; we'll include recommended retention and export configuration in the runbook.
[18:00] Nina: Pricing — high level, what's the expected delta between running 7B quantized vs 13B unquantized on a dedicated pool?
[18:25] Oliver: Ballpark: quantized 7B can be 3-5x cheaper per-token than a 13B float variant, but depends on sequence length and KV cache effectiveness. We'll run a projection for your workload.
[21:00] Tom: Also integrating with our feature flags and rollout — we need canary and automatic fallback if latency spikes. Do you have built-in rollouts and A/B?
[21:20] Maya: Yes — Redwood Console supports canary deployments, percentage rollouts, and automatic fallback policies to cheaper or smaller model variants if SLOs breach. We'll document the rollback triggers.
[28:00] Leah: Networking specifics — we'll need to exchange IP allowlists and certs. Can we get your egress ip ranges?
[28:30] Oliver: I'll share the published egress ranges and the networking checklist. For private peering we work with your network team and provide Terraform snippets.
[35:00] Raj: Data residency question — if we ingest customer transcripts, can we ensure they never leave our VPC and that keys are customer-managed?
[35:25] Oliver: For Private deployments yes, model execution stays in your environment. Control plane metadata can be optionally disabled, and keys can be integrated via your KMS/HSM so we don't have plaintext access.
[40:00] Maya: Recap of next steps — I'll share security packet and network diagram by Thursday 11/18; Oliver will run cost/latency projections and publish an initial benchmark plan; Leah will send traces; Raj will confirm KMS constraints. We'll aim to lock the pilot week (Dec 6-10).
[42:00] Tom: Sounds good. One last thing — can we do a technical deep dive with your SEs on model quantization and batching strategies next week?
[42:15] Oliver: Absolutely — I can set up a 60-minute session and bring in one of our runtime engineers.
[44:12] Maya: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.
